title: Data Center Restrictions Lead 29 to 1 in Initial US Local Ballot Counts
summary:
Local voters in several U.S. states have cast strong opposition to the expansion of AI infrastructure, with restrictions favored in 29 of the first 30 reported ballot measures nationwide. The results show deep resistance to the buildout in Ohio, where 77.4% of Trenton voters backed a data center ban, and in Illinois, where a moratorium on large facilities won 78.8% support in Bloomington. In Janesville, Wisconsin, more than 61% of voters backed a requirement for public approval for projects exceeding $450M at a proposed campus site.

The non-binding votes are part of a total of 41 initiatives across 10 states, reflecting a surge in local opposition that saw the number of U.S. data center bans grow from 40 at the start of 2026 to over 500 by August. The political headwind arrives as the industry contends with state-level permitting and power constraints, including a 474 GW electricity interconnection queue in Texas, roughly 90% of which is driven by data center demand.

selectedTweets.bestBit: In Bloomington, Illinois, 78.8% backed an advisory call for a moratorium on large data centers.
selectedTweets.text:
Support for bans on new data centers is HUGE.

• Trenton, OH: 77.4%
• Urbana, OH: 77.3%
• Edgewater, FL: 77.2%
• Hubbard, OH: 76.6%
• Pataskala, OH: 72.4%
• Piqua, OH: 67.8%
• Defiance, OH: 62.6%
• Emporia, KS: 60.1%

Illinois voters are sending the same message through nonbinding advisory questions. Votes AGAINST supporting new data centers:

• Chouteau Township: 83.3%
• Joliet Township: 78.4%
• Nameoki Township: 77.9%
• Venice Township: 75.9%
• Granite City Township: 74.4%. 

In Bloomington, Illinois, 78.8% backed an advisory call for a moratorium on large data centers. In Ashville, Ohio, 82.5% voted AGAINST the negotiating framework for an EdgeConneX project involving two data center buildings and a natural gas power facility.

Voters are also demanding direct control over development:

• Grove City, OH: 55.1% backed requiring voter approval for projects meeting specified acreage, electricity or water-use thresholds.
• Janesville, WI: 61.6% backed requiring voter approval for projects exceeding $450 million at the former GM/JATCO site, where an $8 billion data center campus has been proposed.

selectedTweets.bestBit: The next governor inherits a 474 GW interconnection queue, roughly 90% of it data centers and more than five times the all-time system peak.
selectedTweets.text:
BofA calls Texas "the single most consequential election for [Data Centers], utilities and power this cycle." The next governor inherits a 474 GW interconnection queue, roughly 90% of it data centers and more than five times the all-time system peak.

"Consensus holds that Abbott reverts to a pro data center stance after a win, and that may prove correct on rhetoric, but the audit, the CCN remands, and the legislative docket now carry institutional momentum independent of the governor. Texas remains the clearest secular demand growth story in the sector, but we would carry materially wider volatility margins for potential outcomes than the market currently reflects." - BofA
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText: BofA's economists think "the biggest downside risks centers around data center regulation," and that it will be decided far from Washington: "Under any plausible election outcome, the President should retain the ability to veto legislation he opposes," which leaves "state and local governments, which control zoning, land use, permitting and development agreements" as "the more immediate constraint."
